description: This bar chart, from the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models,” illustrates the “effect” (y-axis, ranging from 0 to 20 with major ticks at intervals of 5) of different multilingual BERT models across four morphosyntactic categories: “case,” “gender,” “number,” and “tense,” labeled along the x-axis under the overarching label “tag.” Each category contains six grouped bars, each representing a different model variant: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red), as indicated in the legend in the upper right. Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. In the “case” category, mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ show the highest effects (~12–13), while other models range from ~2 to ~6. In “gender,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ again lead (~4–5), with others near or below 2. For “number,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ are again highest (~3), while others are near 1. In “tense,” all models show very low effects, mostly near 0, with slight positive values for mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ (~0.5–1). The bars are not sorted by height within each group, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding. The chart uses a linear y-axis and categorical x-axis, with no gridlines beyond horizontal ones at each 5-unit interval.
